text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak arrives in Washington at the start of his trip to the United States and will meet with U.S. President Bill Clinton. Mubarak and French President Jacques Chirac had agreed in their talks in Paris on the need for a just and comprehensive peace.
Mubarak wants resumption of talks on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks and for America to continue its mediating role.
- Minister of State for Economic Affairs Youssef Boutros-Ghali says that Mubarak's visit to the U.S. also has important economic aims.

- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says in Washington that Egypt sees the U.S. role as active in getting the peace process back on the right track. The talks in Washington will focus on bilateral ties, increasing investment, and international issues.
- 875 million pounds worth of turnover was carried out in the stock exchange last week, and shares of 62 companies rose.
- Mubarak will visit Paris next May to take part in the opening with French President Jacques Chirac of the largest exhibition of Egyptian artefacts ever in the French capital.
- Economic report says that the proportion of investment from the United States is no more than 3.5 percent of all investment projects in Egypt.
